title: Pass full decision graph to pre-edit grounding to surface cross-file topic collisions
context: Agents need to see the complete picture of contested topics before writing code. `renderGrounding` was filtering decisions per-topic/file, so if two decisions contested the same topic across different files, the agent saw only one and treated it as settled—risking accidental re-decisions of already-contested ground. Touches invariant(s): con_902759b3dc (All JSON writes to .hunch/ must be atomic (temp-file + rename) so an interrupted write can never truncate the index); con_a87360128b (Semantic vectors are a derived layer in SQLite, never the source of truth; reconcile by content hash on reindex); con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Changed `renderGrounding` to receive both file-scoped decisions AND the full decision set from the store. Topic collisions across files are now reported as UNRESOLVED with both decision IDs and a reconciliation pointer, rather than silently appearing settled.
consequences: Agents see the full conflict picture before writing code, eliminating false settlement
Ambiguous topics are named rather than hidden—reduces collision-driven re-decisions
Cross-file awareness in grounding increases context passed to pre-edit hook
Topics explicitly marked UNRESOLVED point to `hunch reconcile-topics` for human settlement
alternatives_rejected: Filter decisions at file level only (causes false settlement when collision spans files)
Drop both sides of a collision (loses information about what was contested)
Silence collisions entirely (turns a named uncertainty into a hidden trap)
